conviction_note: No unpriced company-level number found. A revision driven by the yen is very likely at this print: the full-year plan assumes 130 yen to the dollar against about 158 actual, and the company revised at the H1 print last year using the same 130 assumption for H2. But IFIS consensus operating profit of 18.07bn already sits about 30% above the 14.0bn plan, and the company's own calculation at 150.8 yen puts it at 19.2bn. A revision that books H1 at the actual rate but keeps H2 at 130 probably lands at or below consensus. Against that: the last three H1 prints fell (-6.5, -14.9, -20.1), and margin longs are crowded at 7.52x. So abs_move is 7.0 (the real reaction median is about 6.9 and a guidance revision is likely) and p_up is 47, which gives -0.42. The findings sum to +0.2 because the yen revision and the data-centre CPU demand carry small positive sizes, and the reaction-function lean sits in p_up rather than in a finding.
bar: IFIS consensus FY3/2027 operating profit 18,067m JPY, ordinary 18,280m, revenue 231,717m (kabuyoho/IFIS, unchanged for four weeks as of 2026-10-27: https://kabuyoho.jp/sp/reportAnalyst?bcode=6526). Company plan: OP 14,000m, revenue 215,000m, at 130 JPY/USD (https://www.socionext.com/jp/ir/pdf/sn_ir20260729_02j.pdf p.16; the company's own figure at 150.8 yen is OP 19.2bn, revenue 235.8bn). No H1 company forecast is published. print_vs_bar_pct is my estimate of the revised full-year OP guide (about 17bn, with H1 booked at actual FX and H2 left at 130) against the 18.07bn consensus. Only one consensus source (IFIS), so every size is kept small.
positioning_check: JPX disclosed short register as of 2026-10-27: 1.65% of shares out over 2 sellers, up from 1.51% (+0.14pt, building slightly) (https://www.jpx.co.jp/markets/public/short-selling/index.html via baseline). Margin ratio (信用倍率) 7.52x, a crowded margin long (kabutan https://kabutan.jp/stock/finance?code=6526, 2026-10-28). Kabutan/Minkabu 2026-09-24 reported heavy stock-borrow shorting by foreign brokers, partly covered in a 13% squeeze into the September half-year end (https://kabutan.jp/stock/news?code=6526&b=n202609240346). Nomura's large-holding filings keep rising (No.63, 2026-10-21), probably lending-related. No options and no skew. Run-up: -6.94% over 20 days, +5.27% over 5 days, and +3.4% intraday on 10-28 in a semiconductor rally. priced_lean_pct +0.62.

findings.finding: The FY3/27 plan (OP 14.0bn, revenue 215bn) assumes 130 JPY/USD while Q1 averaged 159.5 and spot is about 158. The stated sensitivity is about 1bn of revenue and 0.25bn of OP per yen a year, so H1 alone carries about +3.5bn of OP from FX. Last year the company revised at the H1 print (2025-10-31), booking actual H1 FX but keeping H2 at 130. A headline upward revision is therefore likely at this release, but it probably lands at or below the 18.07bn IFIS consensus, which already prices FX.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: H1 prints: 2023-10-31 raised OP 22.5->29bn, stock -6.5%; 2024-10-31 held, -14.9%; 2025-10-31 raised revenue 175->190bn on FX/demand but cut OP 14->10bn, -20.1% (Yahoo closes, release-day close to next close). Upward guidance has not been bought at H1.
findings.why_not_priced: The FX gap itself is priced: consensus at 18.07bn is already about 30% above the plan. What is not priced is how the company books it. If the market expected the company to adopt market FX for H2, consensus would sit at or above the company's own 19.2bn at 150.8 yen, and it does not. The residual is the retail read of a '上方修正' headline in a register crowded long on margin.
findings.independence: Precedent for the method: the 2025-10-31 revision notice states H2 FX was kept at 130 yen (https://www.socionext.com/jp/ir/pdf/sn_ir20251031_01j.pdf). Consensus level from IFIS (https://kabuyoho.jp/sp/reportAnalyst?bcode=6526).

findings.finding: The company has already said H1 operating margin may come in slightly below its initial assumption (NRE timing, R&D). R&D stays at Q1's level of about 17bn a quarter, product gross margin fell on advanced-node reticle amortisation, and the roughly 10bn of automotive product sales shifted into Q2 is low-margin. So Q2 revenue will look strong year on year while OP stays thin.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY3/27 (2026-07-29): revenue +13% but an operating loss, stock -6.4% the next session and down to -10% intraday. Q4 FY3/26 (2026-04-28): -7.5%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the company said it in July and the stock fell 6-10% on Q1. It stays filed because Q2's own margin print is not yet public, but it lands inside what management guided, so it is sized near 0.
findings.independence: Q1 presentation slide 15 (https://www.socionext.com/jp/ir/pdf/sn_ir20260729_02j.pdf) carries the same statement. Same company, a second document.

findings.finding: Positioning into the print: margin longs are crowded at 7.52x and disclosed shorts are building slightly (+0.14pt to 1.65%). That gives a visible holder base that sold the last three prints (-7.5, -6.4, and -20.1 at last year's H1) and that has to sell any disappointment against the 18bn consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Of 12 real release dates since 2023-10, 7 fell and 4 of the last 6 fell by 6% or more (Yahoo daily closes, https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/6526.T?range=3y&interval=1d).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the disclosed short is small (1.65%), so this is not squeeze fuel. The crowded margin long is the setup in which a miss still has sellers. If it were fully held, the ratio would have unwound after the July fall, and it has not.
findings.independence: JPX short register via baseline (https://www.jpx.co.jp/markets/public/short-selling/index.html). The baseline's own lean component margin_overhang is -0.44.

findings.finding: Management said at the Q1 call that North American data-centre CPU demand is firm, and that customer volumes are now expected above the volumes assumed when the deal was won. H2 product ramps (North American automotive and data-centre) are the stated driver of the back-loaded plan, and the H1 print is where the company comments on H2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2023-10 H1 print carried a raise and fell 6.5%. Forward commentary has not lifted this stock at H1 prints in the last three years.
findings.why_not_priced: The statement is public, and the CPU theme (Meta 'Muse') is in the tape: Nikkei 2026-10-08, https://www.nikkei.com/article/DGXZQOUB30C0R0Q6A930C2000000/. If it were fully priced, the stock would not be 7% down over 20 days during a CPU-led AI rally. The residual is whether the company quantifies higher H2 volumes in this release.
findings.independence: Nikkei 2026-10-08 on CPU-related stocks drawing money (a theme, not company-level): https://www.nikkei.com/article/DGXZQOUB30C0R0Q6A930C2000000/

bar_hierarchy: Forecast revision: likely, driven by FX (130 yen plan against about 158 actual). Last year's precedent books H1 at actual FX and keeps H2 at 130, so the OP guide probably lands about 16-17.5bn against the 18.07bn IFIS consensus. Returns: none expected; dividend fixed at 25 yen interim and no buyback precedent at H1. New-year guide: not applicable at H1. Quarter against own progress rate: H1 ordinary profit was 2,792m last year, 31% of the then-plan (19.9% of the 14bn original). This year Q1 was -782m (-5.6% of plan), so the year is more back-loaded than last year, which the company flagged.

baseline_tension: The findings are close to flat and do not beat the +0.62 priced lean. The strongest positive the release could carry is an upward revision to FX-adjusted guidance with H2 FX also moved toward market, which would put OP at 19bn or more against an 18.07bn consensus. I looked for it, and the precedent says the company keeps H2 at 130. Against it are a crowded margin long and an H1 reaction record of -6.5/-14.9/-20.1.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (a negative resting on a series the market already has): the H1 margin warning has been public since July, so that finding moved from -0.3 to -0.2.

Open question 4 (a five-day run-in read as a short signal went wrong once): the +5.3% five-day run-in was removed from the positioning finding's rationale, which moved from -0.6 to -0.4; p_up moved from 46 to 47.
Rule 2 (check the sign when negatives dominate): two negatives and two positives; the strongest positive is written in baseline_tension and was searched for. No further change.
